title: Making weekend plans
situation: A friend texts you to see if you want to hang out this weekend.
tip: With friends, keep replies short and toss back a question (왜?, 뭐 볼까?) to keep the conversation rolling.

turns.en: What are you up to this weekend?

turns.prompt: Say nothing's planned and ask why.

choices.feedback: Natural — 왜? bounces it back and keeps the chat going.
Too formal for a friend. Drop to 반말: 별거 없어.
That ends the conversation instead of continuing it.

turns.prompt: Agree happily and ask what to watch.

choices.en: Sounds good! What should we watch?
choices.feedback: 좋아 + a follow-up question is exactly how friends keep momentum.
That shuts the plan down — fine if true, but not 'keeping it going'.
Doesn't actually answer the invitation.

turns.prompt: Confirm Saturday and say you'll text later.

choices.en: Saturday evening works. I'll text you later!
choices.feedback: This confirms the proposed evening, and 이따 톡할게 is a natural casual sign-off.
Stiff. With a friend: 토요일 좋아.
Way too formal to end a chat with a friend.

title: Deciding what to eat
situation: You and a friend are hanging out and getting hungry.
tip: 땡기다 (to crave), 콜 (deal!), and 가자 (let's go) are everyday casual staples between friends.

turns.en: I'm hungry… what should we eat?

turns.prompt: Say you don't mind and ask what they're craving.

choices.en: Anything's fine. What are you craving?
choices.feedback: 넌 뭐 땡겨? is very natural casual Korean for 'what do you feel like?'.
Correct grammar, but too formal among friends.
읍시다 is stiff — friends say 먹자.

turns.prompt: Love the idea and suggest a place.

choices.ko: 오 좋아! 학교 앞 거기 갈까?
choices.en: Oh nice! Should we go to that place by school?
choices.feedback: Enthusiasm + a concrete suggestion keeps the plan moving.
A fact, but it doesn't move the plan forward.
This neither accepts nor rejects the suggestion, and -요 mismatches the close-friend register.
가자 is the casual 'let's go' — perfect.
Too formal — 가자 fits a friend.
Over-polite for a close friend.

title: Reacting to a friend's news
situation: A friend excitedly texts you that they saw a celebrity.
tip: Reactions (헐, 대박, 부럽다) plus a quick question (누구?, 사진 찍었어?) are the heart of casual Korean chatting.

turns.en: I saw a celebrity on the street today!

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask who it was.

choices.feedback: 헐 진짜? (reaction) + 누구? (follow-up) is textbook casual chatting.
Flat and formal — friends react bigger than this.
Doesn't fit — there's nothing to congratulate.

turns.en: IU! I saw her at a cafe lol

turns.prompt: Show you're jealous and ask if they got a photo.

choices.en: No way, I'm jealous… did you take a photo?
choices.feedback: 대박 + 부럽다 + a follow-up keeps the energy up.
Too formal — just say 사진 찍었어?
요 is a touch formal, and it turns the spotlight onto you.

turns.en: Of course lol I'll show you later

choices.feedback: 완전 + 기대된다 is natural casual excitement.

choices.en: I will look forward to it (formal).
choices.feedback: Stiff — friends say 기대된다.
Cold and formal for a fun chat.
